value.body: A professional teacher-education degree taken after a bachelor's or master's degree. It covers child development, teaching methods for two school subjects, assessment and a school internship. Programmes must be recognised by the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE).

items.label: Course length
items.note: NCTE Regulations, 2014; includes a school internship

items.label: Minimum marks to apply
items.value: 50% in a bachelor's or master's degree
items.note: Relaxation for reserved categories as per state / central rules

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's or master's degree with the minimum marks set by NCTE. Admission is through state B.Ed entrance tests, university entrance tests (some central universities use CUET-PG) or merit, depending on the state and institution.

value.title: At a glance
items: To teach in most schools you also need to clear a Teacher Eligibility Test (CTET or a state TET) and then a recruitment exam.
A 2023 Supreme Court judgment held that B.Ed holders are not eligible for primary (Classes 1–5) teacher posts under NCTE norms; B.Ed mainly leads to upper-primary and secondary posts.
NEP 2020 envisages the four-year integrated B.Ed (ITEP) as the minimum teacher qualification by 2030, so the two-year route may change.
Quality varies widely across a very large number of private colleges; checking NCTE recognition before admission matters.
